_note: A word is placed by its row in 'layouts' (the main grid) or, on a category page, by its row group in 'groups'. Never move an entry: a word's location is permanent on each grid size. Rows 1-4 of the 84 board are identical to the 45 board; the 45 board's bottom row (yes, no, Chat, categories) is the 84 board's bottom row in the same columns. On the main board 'stage' controls when a word is revealed (shown if stage <= the learner's stage). CATEGORY PAGES are organized by ROW GROUPS: each group is one row (the same row index on both sizes). Its 'words' go in columns 0-8 in order (these are the 45-board words, and the first nine words of the 84 board); its 'adds' go in columns 9-11 and appear on the 84 board only. If the page's Back button sits in that row on the 45 board, the Back column is skipped on BOTH sizes. A word given as {"id": ..., "sizes": [45]} is on the 45 board only. On the 84 board rows 5 and 6 of every page are left empty for the adult's own words. 'starter' lists the original items of a page: they show whenever the page is open. Every other item on a page is a newer word that shows at stage 'pageNewWordStage' and up (an adult can force-show it). A page without groups (Favorites) fills its 'items' left to right, top to bottom, skipping the Back cell. A word with a 'template' speaks that sentence; ___ is a blank an adult fills in. THE WORDS PAGES (Phase 1.6B) use the same row groups. The menu page 'words' has "fromBar": true: it is opened by the Words button in the top bar (not by a grid button), has no Back cell, and its buttons (ids starting w-) open the word pages (depth 2, Back where the button is). 'starter': 'all' means every word on the page always shows. A word with no 'image' is a text-first button (the word is drawn large; the picture area stays, empty). Several words reuse an existing id (for example in, on, he, she, me, my, big, hot): one id is one word, wherever it appears. Every Dolch word must be reachable in 3 taps on both sizes: run tools/dolch-coverage.py after changing a page.
